management_text: Three equal units, short from 7380.18. Stop 7416.98 (+36.80 pts from entry, -1R). Unit 1 exits TP1 7332.87 (-47.31 pts, +1.29R, daily S1). Unit 2 exits TP2 7313.15 (-67.03 pts, +1.82R, the S1/S2 midpoint); on that fill Unit 3 stop moves to entry + 0.2R = 7387.54 (+7.36 pts). Unit 3 traces to TP3 7293.43 (-86.75 pts, +2.36R, daily S2) or to the trailed stop, whichever comes first; there is no session time-stop on this branch. R = 36.80 pts = 0.31 x ATR(14) 117.90 (14 cash sessions ending 24 Jun 2026), so the ratio is below 1.00 and no wide-stop flag is set; 2R = 73.60 is far inside 3 x ATR(14) = 353.70, so no 'ambitious TP2' flag. Thesis invalidation, distinct from the stop and 31.55 pts inside it: a daily close back above the daily pivot 7385.43, which negates the sub-pivot posture the card trades; the stop sits beyond the invalidation, so the position can be stopped before the thesis is formally broken. Confluences: entry 7380.18 sits 5.26 pts (0.04 x ATR) below the daily pivot 7385.43 - strong confluence; stop 7416.98 sits 7.89 pts (0.07 x ATR) below daily R1 7424.87 - strong confluence, and 21.02 pts below the 24 Jun session high 7438.00; TP1 is daily S1 exactly; TP2 is the S1/S2 midpoint and sits 7.32 pts (0.06 x ATR) below the prior-week S2 7320.47 - strong confluence; TP3 is daily S2 exactly. Caveats: the daily pivot tiers are flagged single-source-indicative in the source-discipline section of the report, and that qualifier is carried here (the weekly tier is corroborated, so the all-tiers-indicative suppression trigger does not fire); the levels above are computed from the slice's 24 Jun cash session H 7438.00 / L 7346.00 / C 7372.30 and not from the report's price table, which is systematically 6 to 40 pts low. The card's one-session horizon collides with a high-impact US data block scheduled 15:30 broker on 25 Jun - Core PCE Price Index m/m and y/y, GDP q/q, Durable Goods Orders m/m and Initial Jobless Claims - one hour before the cash open, so the entry can be gapped through in either direction.
rationale: Regime: the report calls the composite label TRANSITION - its regime section closes with 'the composite consolidated label is therefore TRANSITION, not a clean RANGE' and its agent log repeats 'Composite regime: TRANSITION'. The dual gate for a clean range read needs an overlap ratio above 0.55 and a non-expanding volatility slope; the report has overlap 0.58 (passes) and slope +0.07, expanding (fails), so only the transition branch is available. Under that label the only permitted pivot card is a breakout-side entry aligned with the breakout direction, and a counter-side limit fade at resistance is not available - which is why the report's published sell limit into R1 with 1R/2R targets is not reproduced here. Breakout side: down. The report's directional conviction is negative, its cross-asset read is CONFIRM (bearish, two of three confirming, none contradicting), its forecast is 'mild downward bias', its regime section names 'a clean break of 7347' as the resolving event, and the 24 Jun close settled below the daily pivot; every one of those points the break side downward, so the card is short and takes the support-side pivot ladder. Reference close: 7372.30, the settled cash-session close of Wednesday 24 June 2026, the last completed session strictly before D = 25 June 2026. ATR(14) = 117.90 index points on the 14 completed cash sessions ending 24 Jun 2026, true range = max(H-L, |H-Cprev|, |L-Cprev|); this is the declared cash-session bar basis the report's own market definition fixes, and it is the basis every buffer, cap and flag on this card is a multiple of. On full broker-day bars the same window gives 130.02; that figure is not the card basis and is quoted only because the static checker recomputes on it. Daily floor pivots from the D-1 (24 Jun) cash session H 7438.00 / L 7346.00 / C 7372.30: P = (H+L+C)/3 = 7385.43; R1 = 2P - L = 7424.87; R2 = P + (H-L) = 7477.43; R3 = H + 2(P-L) = 7516.87; S1 = 2P - H = 7332.87; S2 = P - (H-L) = 7293.43; S3 = L - 2(H-P) = 7240.87. The S1/S2 midpoint used as TP2 is (7332.87 + 7293.43)/2 = 7313.15. Prior-week pivots from the last fully completed week 15-19 Jun (H 7583.40, L 7408.50, C 7494.20): P 7495.37, R1 7582.23, S1 7407.33, S2 7320.47 - used for confluence only. Entry: the downside breakout trigger of the pivot band, P - 0.10 x (P - S1) = 7385.43 - 0.10 x 52.57 = 7380.18. Because the 24 Jun close settled at 7372.30, 7.88 pts below that trigger, the order rests as a sell limit rather than a sell stop; a sell limit is required to sit at or above the reference close and it does. Stop: the branch rule places it 80% of the way from the pivot up toward R1, P + 0.80 x (R1 - P) = 7385.43 + 0.80 x 39.43 = 7416.98. The structural alternative - just beyond R1 plus a 0.25 x ATR(14) buffer, 7424.87 + 29.48 = 7454.35 - is wider, and the rule takes whichever is tighter, so 7416.98 stands. R = 7416.98 - 7380.18 = 36.80 pts = 0.31 x ATR(14) on the card's declared cash basis, inside the 0.3 x ATR (35.37) to 3.0 x ATR (353.70) band. On the static checker's full-broker-day ATR of 130.02 the same 36.80 reads 0.28x and will draw a tiny-R warning; that is a bar-basis artefact, not a construction defect, and the rule leaves no room to widen it - both the entry and the stop are fixed functions of the same three pivots, the only permitted alternative stop is wider but is excluded by the explicit 'whichever is tighter' clause, and moving either level to manufacture a larger R would break the branch geometry. Targets are the branch's structural pivot ladder, not R-multiples: TP1 = S1 = 7332.87, TP2 = the S1/S2 midpoint = 7313.15, TP3 = S2 = 7293.43. Ladder order for a short holds: stop 7416.98 > entry 7380.18 > TP1 7332.87 > TP2 7313.15 > TP3 7293.43. TP1 sits 47.31 pts from entry, well inside the 2.5 x ATR(14) reachability band of 294.75 (325.05 on the full-day basis). No fib percentage is used on this card; the fib construction belongs to the Trade 3 family. Where the report disagreed with the slice: the report's 24 Jun H/L/C of 7424.50 / 7355.80 / 7358.22 produce P 7379.51 and R1 7403.21, and its card was built on those; the slice's 24 Jun cash session is H 7438.00 / L 7346.00 / C 7372.30, which moves the pivot up 5.92 pts and R1 up 21.66 pts, so entry, stop and every target here differ from the published card. The report's regime section states 'the composite consolidated label is therefore TRANSITION, not a clean RANGE' and its agent log repeats 'Composite regime: TRANSITION'; that label maps to the momentum-breakout variant, not to the momentum-pullback variant the report published. The mapping carries no discretion, and a variant whose own eligibility test fails is suppressed rather than replaced by a different variant or by pivot levels standing in for range levels. Range definition, from the 25 completed cash sessions ending 24 Jun 2026: high 7624.60 (02 Jun 2026), low 7243.10 (09 Jun 2026), width 381.50 pts. The reference close - the settled cash-session close of Wednesday 24 June 2026, 7372.30, the last completed session strictly before D = 25 June 2026 - is 129.20 pts above the range low and 252.30 pts below the range high, so no confirming close exists on either side and the variant is not eligible. Direction is logged as SHORT because that is the break side the report identifies (negative conviction, cross-asset CONFIRM bearish, forecast 'mild downward bias', 'a clean break of 7347 would invalidate the fade and open the lower-range targets'), and the pivot card for this date is aligned to the same side; the direction is recorded for that alignment only and no order follows from it. Had the downside break been confirmed, the construction would have been stop = range low + 0.40 x width = 7243.10 + 152.60 = 7395.70, TP1 = trigger - 1.0 x width and TP2 = trigger - 1.5 x width, with TP1 at 381.50 pts = 3.24 x ATR(14) sitting outside the 2.5 x ATR(14) = 294.75 reachability band - a second reason no such ladder is emitted. The pullback-variant qualifier, tested explicitly because the report published a pullback card: a qualifying swing needs magnitude at least 2 x ATR(14) = 235.80 pts on the cash basis (260.04 on full-day bars) inside the 4-to-10 session adaptive lookback ending 24 Jun 2026. Walking the lookback out one session at a time on the slice's cash sessions gives 4 and 5 sessions 7538.80 (22 Jun) to 7346.00 (24 Jun) = 192.80; 6 sessions 7540.00 (17 Jun) to 7346.00 = 194.00; 7 sessions 7571.40 (16 Jun) to 7346.00 = 225.40; 8 and 9 sessions 7583.40 (15 Jun) to 7346.00 = 237.40; 10 sessions 7583.40 (15 Jun) with the low 7260.00 (11 Jun) preceding it, so the completed leg there is still the 237.40-pt down-leg. Nothing inside the 4-to-7 session window qualifies, the deepest 8-to-10 session leg clears the cash threshold by 1.60 pts and fails the full-day threshold of 260.04 outright, and the swing the report actually anchored on - 7511.07 down to 7347.60, 163.47 pts, and on the slice 7538.80 down to 7346.00, 192.80 pts - fails the 2 x ATR test on every basis. The pullback variant is in any case not the fork this regime selects, so it is not emitted; the 57.5% retracement entry, 38.2% first target and 0% second target that the report's card claimed are not reproduced, and the card it published was in fact a stop order on a break of the prior session low, which is breakout geometry under a pullback heading.
